claims.text: The early stages of oxidation in equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn are governed by differences in the intrinsic atomic sizes of its constituent elements.
The early stages of oxidation in equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn are governed by differences in the redox potentials of its constituent elements.
Differences in atomic size and redox potential cause rapid formation of a heterogeneous oxide film.
At high oxygen partial pressure and elevated temperature, the heterogeneous oxide film undergoes a composition-inversion process.
Composition inversion converts the heterogeneous film into a continuous, multicomponent protective oxide layer.
The continuous multicomponent oxide layer enhances oxidation resistance and sustains material integrity.
The composition and structure of the oxide scale reflect the individual elemental redox potentials.
The composition and structure of the oxide scale reflect the individual elemental atomic sizes.
Elements with lower redox potentials preferentially oxidize during initial exposure.
Elements with smaller atomic sizes preferentially oxidize during initial exposure.
Diffusion and interfacial reactions at increased oxygen partial pressure and sustained high temperature drive composition inversion.
Composition inversion produces a uniform and adherent protective oxide layer.
The resulting protective oxide layer limits further oxygen ingress.
Increasing oxygen partial pressure will systematically promote evolution from an initially nonuniform oxide film to a continuous protective scale.
Oxidation at ambient oxygen partial pressure will produce less controlled oxide speciation than oxidation at higher oxygen partial pressure.
Oxidation at ambient oxygen partial pressure will produce more defects and nonprotective regions than oxidation at higher oxygen partial pressure.
The defective oxide formed at ambient oxygen partial pressure will correlate with inferior material integrity.
The proposed hypothesis is expected to apply between 800 and 1200 degrees Celsius under variable oxygen partial pressures.

contradictions.description: The intervention and conditions describe ambient oxygen as a baseline measured with real-time in-situ characterization, whereas the baseline field defines the ambient test as being conducted without added spectroscopic monitoring. Thus, the baseline is specified inconsistently and is not measurement-matched to the higher-pressure conditions.
